questions.prompt: Choose the word or phrase which best completes each sentence."Will you come to the party tomorrow?" – "I will if I ______ no visitors."

options.explain: correct — present simple in a first-conditional if-clause
wrong tense for an if-clause referring to the future
wrong aspect for this general condition

options.explain: correct — "ask someone not to do something"

doesn't fit the fixed phrase "had better"

questions.prompt: Choose the word or phrase which best completes each sentence.Everybody in both cars ______ injured in the accident last night.

wrong agreement and tense — "everybody" is singular

questions.prompt: Choose the word or phrase which best completes each sentence.______ to have lunch with us today?

questions.prompt: Choose the word or phrase which best completes each sentence.Let's go out for a walk, ______?

questions.prompt: Choose the word or phrase which best completes each sentence.Drinking and smoking will do great harm ______ people's health.

options.explain: correct — "do harm to" is the fixed collocation

questions.prompt: Choose the word or phrase which best completes each sentence.He always ______.

options.explain: not a finite verb form after "always"

questions.prompt: Choose the word or phrase which best completes each sentence.My parents are going to take three days ______ next month to help my brother move his house.

options.explain: correct — "take days off" is the fixed collocation for time away from work

questions.prompt: Choose the word or phrase which best completes each sentence.In my class, Trung was responsible ______ the teacher ______ keeping the class in order while she went out.
Choose the word or phrase which best completes each sentence.The scheme allows students from many countries to communicate ______.

options.explain: wrong meaning — implies talking to oneself
grammatically fine, but "with one another" is the more standard choice for 3+ people/countries
correct — "one another" for interaction among many (multiple countries)

questions.prompt: Choose the word or phrase which best completes each sentence.Have you ever read anything ______ Earnest Hemingway?
Choose the word or phrase which best completes each sentence.Not a good movie, ______?

options.explain: wrong polarity — needs a positive tag after this negative statement
correct — positive tag matching the implicit "it was not"

questions.prompt: Choose the word or phrase which best completes each sentence.Hurry up! They have only got ______ seats left.

options.explain: correct — "a few" with a countable plural noun, fitting the urgency
wrong — "a little" pairs with uncountable nouns, not "seats"
